articles.title: “If you see Charles Barkley, arrest him”: Newly minted FBI special agent Shaquille O’Neal targets Inside the NBA co-host to put behind bars in a humorous jab
articles.summary: NBA News: Shaquille O'Neal picked up an honorary FBI special agent title, and the four-time NBA champion wasted no time putting it to use. He graduated alongsid.
articles.body: Shaquille O'Neal picked up an honorary FBI special agent title, and the four-time NBA champion wasted no time putting it to use. He graduated alongside 265 law enforcement officials at the FBI National Academy's Session 299 in Quantico, Virginia, then closed his speech with a warning aimed squarely at his longtime broadcast partner.FBI Director Kash Patel handed O'Neal the recognition once the ten-week program wrapped. O'Neal turned the moment into a shot at Charles Barkley, the co-host he has jabbed at on Inside the NBA since 2011, telling the room what to do if they ever ran into him.Shaquille O'Neal targets Charles Barkley in his honorary FBI special agent speechShaquille O'Neal's parting line was simple. "If you see Charles Barkley, arrest him," he said, in video shared by Legion Hoops as he wrapped his remarks Thursday. The crowd of graduating officers, all veterans of their own departments, got the joke instantly given O'Neal and Barkley's decade-plus history of ribbing each other on air.Patel had announced the honor on X a day earlier, calling O'Neal "one of the best supporters of law enforcement in the country" as he presented the plaque. The title carries no real authority. It does not make O'Neal a sworn agent or give him powers of arrest, and the National Academy itself runs separately from the FBI's actual new-agent training pipeline. It exists mainly for experienced law enforcement leaders, covering leadership, academics and physical fitness over ten weeks in Quantico.Shaquille O'Neal's law enforcement ties run back two decadesThis is not O'Neal dabbling. He was sworn in as a Miami Beach reserve police officer in 2005, not long after serving in the same capacity with the Los Angeles Port Police. That same year, during his reserve training, he tailed a car whose passengers had thrown a bottle at two pedestrians, then radioed dispatch so officers could track down the suspect. He later took on a reserve role in Doral, Florida, and was named Henry County Police Department's community relations chief last year.Orlando drafted him first overall in 1992, and he spent 19 seasons across six teams, winning three titles with the Lakers and one with the Heat, taking home MVP honors in 2000 and making 15 All-Star teams before his 2016 Hall of Fame induction. But the badge, honorary or not, fits a pattern he has kept up since long before Inside the NBA made him a household name twice over.As for Barkley, he has not responded publicly yet. Given their on-air history, a comeback is probably just a matter of time.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fever star Kelsey Mitchell breaks A'ja Wilson's WNBA single-season scoring record
articles.summary: The Fever offense has been absurd this year, with Mitchell the leading scorer.
articles.body:
With the WNBA expanding its regular-season schedule to 44 games in 2025 and 2026 , records were bound to be broken. Kelsey Mitchell obliged on Friday.

The Indiana Fever star scored 33 points in a 103-85 win over the Toronto Tempo on Friday , upping her season total to 1,034. That broke the WNBA single-season scoring record set by A'ja Wilson in 2024 (1,021 points when teams played only 40 games).

Mitchell and Caitlin Clark have combined to produce the most lethal offense in WNBA history this season, with the Fever's current mark of 97.1 points per game on pace to shatter the record currently held by the 2010 Phoenix Mercury at 93.9 points per game.

The pair are all over the WNBA's leaderboard. In addition to Mitchell leading the league in total points, Clark ranks third with 837 (with 28 Friday). Clark also ranks second in total assists and is the league leader in assists per game, while Mitchell leads the pack in field goals and 3-point shooting percentage.

Mitchell is also one 3-pointer behind Rhyne Howard , who broke the single-season mark Thursday .

Does the WNBA's schedule expansion water down those achievements? Perhaps to some, but this is common ground in sports history, going back to arguments over whether Roger Maris' record of 61 homers should have come with an asterisk because he did it in 162 games while Babe Ruth's previous record of 60 was done in a 154-game season.

No one bothers denigrating baseball records now because of that schedule shift. It is simply all part of a league's growing pains, as circumstances change and certain numbers become more accessible to athletes.

And with WNBA teams set to play 50 games starting next year, Mitchell's record might not last for long. She might not even have the record at the end of the season.

A'ja Wilson could theoretically reclaim record

Mitchell might have the most points this season, but Wilson is the current leader in points per game. She's just played three fewer games than Mitchell.

Wilson currently sits at 991 points, 43 behind Mitchell. Both players have three games remaining in the regular season and something to play for with WNBA playoff seeding still being decided. Wilson's Las Vegas Aces are currently third in the league at 28-13, but only one game ahead of the Fever and Atlanta Dream .

The Aces' final three games are against the Seattle Storm , Los Angeles Sparks and Phoenix Mercury, three teams that rank no better than eighth in points allowed per game, while the Fever play the Minnesota Lynx twice and the Washington Mystics , who are both in the top three in points allowed per game.

You should probably give the advantage to the player with the 43-point cushion, but it would be inaccurate to say this record is settled. At the very least, Mitchell has some runway to add to an already historic season.

articles.title: New Lakers owners project an astonishing $30 billion valuation in a decade as Luka Doncic’s roster prepares to enter new NBA season
articles.summary: NBA News: The new Lakers owners are telling investors the team's valuation will reach at least $30 billion by the end of 2037. Joshua Kushner and Bob Iger led t.
articles.body: The new Lakers owners are telling investors the team's valuation will reach at least $30 billion by the end of 2037. Joshua Kushner and Bob Iger led the group that bought the franchise for a record $12.5 billion last month, so the pitch aims high, and parts of it will land hard with fans.Across the Atlantic, Luka Doncic is finishing his offseason work in Slovenia, and the latest report on the guard's conditioning is encouraging. Lakers camp opens Sept. 29, less than two weeks away, and the early numbers point the right way.New Lakers owners expect $30 billion valuation in a decadeJoshua Kushner's investment firm, Thrive Capital, built the presentation, and the Wall Street Journal reviewed a copy. It says the Lakers could be worth at least $30 billion by the end of 2037. Television and streaming rights would have to double in value over the same stretch.Revenue is the other half of the story. The pitch says the Lakers are on pace to bring in $681 million this year. Ten years from now, the target is at least $1.6 billion. If conditions break even better, the group reportedly sees a long-term value of $62 billion.Per Yahoo Sports, the $30 billion mark is bigger than the latest Sportico valuations of the Trail Blazers, Timberwolves, Magic, Pistons, Hornets, Pelicans and Grizzlies combined. The owners can also point to some history. Forbes projected the Lakers at $3 billion in 2016, and the $12.5 billion sale price is roughly four times that.The presentation reportedly targets $150 million in extra revenue by 2028. Part of it would come from taking back about 6,000 season tickets now held by brokers and selling them as single-game seats, which would lift the average single-game price from $217 to $361. The owners also reportedly see $40 million to $75 million in new sponsorship money and at least $20 million in operating savings. Yahoo Sports summed it up as pricier tickets, more ads and deeper spending cuts.In public, the owners have promised to "compete at the highest level" and to serve the team, its fans and the city. Thrive also expects the NBA's media deals, now worth $77 billion over 11 years, to double when the current agreement ends.Luka Doncic is ready to enter new NBA season with LakersLuka Doncic has spent the offseason getting his body back in order, and the early signs are good. SportKlub.si, a Slovenian outlet, reports that the Lakers guard weighs about 105 kilograms (231 pounds) as the last stage of the Ljubljana workouts begins. BasketNews passed the report along on Sept. 15. SportKlub put it this way: "His weight is also within the desired range, unofficially even at 105 kilograms."The Lakers listed the 27-year-old at 104 kilograms (230 pounds) last season, so the gap is about one kilogram before camp even starts.Doncic suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain late last season. The injury ended the season and kept him out of the entire Lakers playoff run. The offseason plan began with rehab and then moved into conditioning work.The layoff is a long one. From the final game of last season to the first game of 2026-27, 203 days will pass. It is the longest basketball break of the Slovenian star's career.Doncic did not play for Slovenia this summer and chose family time instead. Basketball still stayed on the schedule. Individual work continued, and Doncic organized a Lakers minicamp in Slovenia.Doncic is expected to stay in Europe until Sept. 20 before flying back to Los Angeles. The Lakers hold media day on Sept. 28, and training camp opens the next day.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Knicks' Jalen Brunson gets positive injury update after offseason wrist surgery
articles.summary: The New York Knicks just got a great update for training camp. Their superstar Jalen Brunson seems to have recovered from his offseason wrist injury just fin...
articles.body:
The New York Knicks are coming off their first NBA championship in over a few decades. They were led by superstar Jalen Brunson , who was a nightmare for the San Antonio Spurs .

"It will be the same. It's something that I get to walk around with and think about when I'm — when I need to give myself a little confidence, or whatever, just in certain situations. But my approach and everything has to be the same. Just because I've reached the mountaintop of winning an NBA championship doesn't mean that it's over with. I feel like there's still a lot more to do and a lot more that I can prove. It's 100 percent always going to be in the mind, I'm just not going to let it define me," Brunson said.

At the end of the Finals run, the MVP had wrist surgery after battling through the playoffs with the injury.

" New York Knicks Finals MVP Jalen Brunson is undergoing surgery on his left wrist and is expected to return to basketball activities later this summer, sources tell ESPN," ESPN's Shams Charania posted.

With training camp coming up, there was some wondering if he would be available. ESPN's Vincent Goodwill gave a great update on Brunson.

"[Jalen Brunson's] at about 80 to 85% after the wrist surgery that he had in July. ... He'll have no restrictions when training camp begins in a couple of weeks," Goodwill said.

The Knicks will likely be very cautious with the way they use Brunson until it gets closer to the season. Brunson isn't at full health yet, but he is pretty close, so he will still be working his way up.

New York has pretty much the same roster from last season, so he doesn't really need to form chemistry with others. There are some veterans who will be fighting for a roster spot, giving him the opportunity to give his input. It is great news that Brunson will be back for training camp with no restrictions.

articles.title: ‘Adorable’ – WNBA fans react to Indiana Fever’s locker room surprise for Kelsey Mitchell
articles.summary: Indiana Fever celebrated Kelsey Mitchell’s record-breaking night in style. The Indiana Fever recently took on the Toronto Tempo, and as expected, it was a on...
articles.body:
Indiana Fever celebrated Kelsey Mitchell 's record-breaking night in style.

The Indiana Fever recently took on the Toronto Tempo , and as expected, it was a one-sided WNBA contest.

Kelsey Mitchell spearheaded the Fever's 103-85 win following a 33-point effort. Aside from Mitchell, Clark also dropped 28 points in a team-high 34 minutes.

However, Mitchell was the star of the show as the MVP candidate broke Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson's phenomenal WNBA record.

WNBA fans react to Indiana Fever showering Kelsey Mitchell with confetti

Mitchell's scoring outburst helped her get past Wilson's 1,021 mark for most points scored in a single WNBA season. Wilson set the record in 2024, and now Mitchell has surpassed it, as she already has 1,023 points in the current campaign.

The Fever star's historic night was made even better by her teammates as she was showered with confetti in the locker room.

"Ok this is adorable," one fan wrote. While another added, "The cleaning crew are not going to be happy in the morning."

"Look at little jumps; Kelsey is a cutie," a third fan pointed out. "The Fever have a great team! Go for the championship!" a fourth fan announced.

"Confetti in the locker room is so unserious; I love it," a fifth fan stated in awe of the moment.

While the majority of fans loved the moment, some questioned the Fever's biased behaviour towards Mitchell.

They demanded answers about why Clark isn't treated the same way despite breaking a plethora of WNBA records each season.

articles.body: El Real Madrid busca conquistar el primer trofeo oficial de la temporada en la gran final de la SuperCup de la Euroliga, cita histórica que estrena palmarés en el Etihad Arena de Abu Dabi. El equipo de Pedro Martínez llega tras superar un exigente choque en semifinales frente al Dubai Basketball (95-98) en la prórroga, haciendo gala de su carácter competitivo e impulsado por el liderazgo de Walter Tavares, Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot, Jaime Pradilla y Gabriel Deck. Los blancos afrontan esta prueba de máxima exigencia para consolidar los mecanismos de sus numerosas incorporaciones estivales y dar continuidad a las buenas sensaciones del nuevo proyecto técnico. En frente estará el poderoso Olympiacos, vigente campeón europeo, que se presenta al duelo de máxima rivalidad tras deshacerse del Fenerbahce en su respectiva semifinal. El conjunto heleno, que cuenta con una plantilla de altísimo nivel reforzada por nombres como Jean Montero, Codi Miller-McIntyre, Evan Fournier o Sasha Vezenkov, reeditará frente a la entidad madridista la final europea más repetida de la historia. Ambos gigantes continentales medirán sus fuerzas en un compromiso de alta intensidad donde la solidez defensiva y la gestión del ritmo de juego resultarán claves para proclamarse primer supercampeón de la Euroliga. articles.title: Caitlin Clark ‘would sign up’ for potential WNBA game overseas after returning from World Cup
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark said she'd sign up for a WNBA overseas game after playing in front of passionate fans at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark may already be prepared for another trip across the ocean. The Indiana Fever star said she would welcome an opportunity to play a WNBA game overseas after recently returning from the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup in Berlin. "I think we’re just scratching the surface of where we can go globally," Clark told reporters following the Fever’s 103-85 victory over the Toronto Tempo on Friday. "I wouldn’t be surprised if next year you see a game played overseas of some sort. I would sign up for that. I think it’d be really good to help expand the WNBA, and I’m looking forward to that." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The WNBA has not announced plans to hold a game in Europe next season, making Clark’s comments a prediction rather than confirmation of a league initiative. Clark made her first appearance in a major international tournament this month while helping the United States win its fifth consecutive World Cup championship. Team USA defeated France 97-79 in the final Sunday in Berlin. The tournament also offered Clark her first extended opportunity to play in Europe. "That was the first time I’ve really played in Europe, and obviously basketball is really loved in Europe," Clark said. "It was fun to get to play in front of those fans." Clark said she was particularly struck by the passion international players displayed while representing their countries. "I think one of the biggest things I took away is how much pride those girls play with, especially the ones that are in the WNBA going to play for their home country," she said. "It means so much to them. I think that’s really cool, and they’ve done so much to help grow the game in their specific countries." WNBA LEGEND BREANNA STEWART OPENS UP ON REPRESENTING AMERICA AT FIBA WOMEN'S WORLD CUP The international influence within the WNBA has already reached record levels. According to the league, 51 foreign-born players had appeared in at least one game during the opening week of the 2026 season, setting a single-season record. A total of 70 current and former WNBA players later appeared on rosters for the World Cup. The league’s geographic footprint has also expanded beyond the United States. The Tempo began play this season as the WNBA’s first Canadian franchise, joining the returning Portland Fire as the league grew to 15 teams. Franchises in Cleveland, Detroit and Philadelphia are scheduled to begin play between 2028 and 2030, eventually bringing the league to 18 teams. The WNBA played its first regular-season game outside the United States in Vancouver in 2025, but a game in Europe would further accelerate its international ambitions. Clark saw evidence of the league’s reach throughout Team USA’s run in Germany. "The amount of young kids and young fans that were super excited to see us was cool," Clark said. Clark returned to WNBA action Friday and recorded 28 points and 14 assists in Indiana’s win over Toronto. Kelsey Mitchell scored 33 points and broke the league’s single-season scoring record during the victory. articles.title: “That’s Very Important In A Leader” – 8-Time WNBA All-Star Shares Drastically Different Take on Cathy Engelbert’s Retirement
articles.summary: Earlier in September, Cathy Engelbert announced that she would retire as WNBA commissioner at the end of this calendar year. Since then, players and experts...
articles.body:
Earlier in September, Cathy Engelbert announced that she would retire as WNBA commissioner at the end of this calendar year. Since then, players and experts have joined the conversation to assess the 61-year-old's performance during her tenure. The newest addition to the list is eight-time WNBA All-Star Tina Charles .

In a recent conversation on Sue Bird 's YouTube podcast , Charles was asked what qualities she wanted in the new WNBA commissioner. However, the New York City native took the conversation to a different angle and had plenty of praise for Engelbert.

Praising Engelbert's contributions to the league's growth and partnerships, Tina Charles said, "Everybody's not perfect, but she definitely did help push us forward, bring us forward. Someone who understands where we're at and where we need to continue to go. Valuing relationships."

"I think it's hard to know what someone needs if you don't have a relationship with them, the level of communication. I think that's very important in a leader."

"But someone who's definitely able to take us even further to see what the product is and make the right adjustments, have those conversations, and then even able to have uncomfortable conversations. That's even important as well."

Since Engelbert's retirement announcement, there has been considerable debate over her stances on various matters. From her views on what a woman should be to the lengthy CBA negotiations, she has frequently been a topic of discussion around the league. However, her tenure as WNBA commissioner certainly coincided with significant growth in the league, and her replacement will be expected to continue the momentum.

Tina Charles Shares Her Thoughts on WNBA Momentum After FIBA World Cup Break

After a 17-day hiatus to accommodate the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup , the WNBA has returned for the final regular-season games. Since a total of 70 current and former league stars featured in the quadrennial event, there is considerable speculation about what impact the tournament will have as the league progresses into the postseason.

While discussing her thoughts on the matter, Tina Charles said, "Everybody's hurt right now. There's a difference between being hurt and there's a difference between being injured."

Charles further shared a piece of advice: "I think for those players, it's just mindset. It's like, hey, you can use it as an excuse. You did have to go over there. You did have to continue to put your body on the line. Or you can take it and continue to play at that level. Continue to see how you could quarantine your teammates of where now you were in their position."

WNBA heads into the playoffs on September 27, 2026. As of this writing, the Minnesota Lynx sit atop the standings with 31 wins, followed by the Golden State Valkyries with 29 wins.

articles.title: New York Knicks’ Jalen Brunson Has Encouraging Injury Update Ahead of Training Camp
articles.summary: The New York Knicks ended their championship drought last season, thanks to Jalen Brunson‘s heroics. However, it came at a cost, as Brunson needed surgery th...
articles.body:
The New York Knicks ended their championship drought last season, thanks to Jalen Brunson 's heroics. However, it came at a cost, as Brunson needed surgery this offseason to address his injured left wrist.

With Brunson hurt, several New York Knicks supporters are concerned. However, on Friday, ESPN's Vince Goodwill shared some good news about the reigning Finals MVP's condition.

"One thing you didn't see about Jalen Brunson's wrist was a brace because he's at about 80 to 85% after the wrist surgery that he had in July. He's back to doing basketball activities. He'll have no restrictions when training camp begins in a couple of weeks, as the Knicks begin their bid to repeat," Goodwill said on NBA Today.

Brunson led the New York Knicks on a dominant playoff run, earning Eastern Conference and Finals MVP awards. In the Finals against the San Antonio Spurs, he averaged 32.6 points, 4.2 rebounds, 4.6 assists, and 2.0 steals on 42.1 percent shooting from the field across five games.

New York Knicks News: Sophomore forward labeled as the team's breakout candidate for 2026-27

Save for Mitchell Robinson, the New York Knicks will bring back most of their championship-winning core this upcoming season. However, they'll likely need some other players to step up to repeat as NBA champions. According to Greg Swartz of Bleacher Report, Mohamed Diawara is poised to have a breakout 2026-27 campaign.

"Regular season fatigue is bound to set in at some point for the defending champion New York Knicks. When it does, the franchise will need players like Mohamed Diawara to help provide a spark. The 6'9″ forward has strong defensive skills that will be called on even more while sharing the second unit with Andre Drummond instead of Mitchell Robinson," Swartz wrote.

"Diawara also connected on 57.6 percent of his corner three-pointers last season, proving to be a reliable kick-out option for Jalen Brunson and others. Diawara's offensive role could slowly expand over time, although most of his impact and breakout will come on the defensive end this season," he ended.

articles.title: Former Washington Wizards Forward Has Unfiltered Take About the Team’s Direction After Offseason Moves
articles.summary: The Washington Wizards are determined to get out of the league’s basement. In the past few months, they acquired Trae Young (eventually giving him a lucrativ...
articles.body:
The Washington Wizards are determined to get out of the league's basement. In the past few months, they acquired Trae Young (eventually giving him a lucrative extension) and Anthony Davis before selecting AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 pick in this summer's NBA Draft.

Despite these moves, Montrezl Harrell remains unconvinced about the Washington Wizards ' chances to compete in 2026-27, as the former NBA journeyman questioned the team's roster construction.

"I don't know what the hell Washington is doing, to be honest with you. They got the young kid AJ Dybantsa, but he's at the three. You bring over Deandre Ayton , but you already drafted the young kid Alex Sarr . Then you have Anthony Davis, but you have another center on the bench in Tristan Vukčević. Now you have four centers because you also have Jonas Valančiūnas. Your only backup to Anthony Davis right now is Anthony Gill , and then you have Trae Young with no legitimate two-guard playing," Harrell told Brandon "Scoop B" Robinson.

"But when you look at that bench, you can beat them with that every night. It's going to be something where the coach is going to have to coach that team. There is a lot of uncertainty down there. I don't see them being in any serious conversation in the East. Maybe they can get into a play-in situation, but I don't see them being a crazy East contender. I just don't know what their team identity is," he ended.

Washington Wizards News: Former NBA guard shares opposing view to Montrezl Harrell's

While Montrezl Harrell is pessimistic about the Washington Wizards this upcoming season, the same can't be said for Darren Collison , who believes they're a dark horse team in the Eastern Conference.

"The Washington Wizards are gonna surprise a lot of people in the East… I think Trae Young is gonna have a really good season. I think Anthony Davis- his ability to protect the paint and be that force down low is gonna take a lot of pressure off of AJ (Dybantsa) just to be the guy. AJ doesn't have to be the guy; AJ is gonna be an added asset," Collison said.

"They have depth. And I always feel that the teams with the most depth have the most success. So they have youth, they have veteran leadership, and they have two guys in Trae Young and AD who have been All-Stars, who have played at a high level in the playoffs," he ended.

articles.title: Sacramento Kings Guard Pays Touching Tribute to Russell Westbrook After Retirement Announcement
articles.summary: Russell Westbrook caught everyone by surprise when he announced his retirement from the NBA after suiting up for the Sacramento Kings, who finished 22-60 las...
articles.body:
Russell Westbrook caught everyone by surprise when he announced his retirement from the NBA after suiting up for the Sacramento Kings , who finished 22-60 last season.

During a recent New Balance event in Boston , Zach LaVine paid tribute to Westbrook in an exclusive interview with ClutchPoints' Tomer Azarly. There, he reflected on having the one-time league MVP as a teammate with the Sacramento Kings .

"I mean, Russ is one of the best humans I've met. The dude has an energy like you've never seen before, and I played against him. I came to the league in 2014, a couple years later, I think he won MVP. It was hell trying to guard him when I was younger, especially when I was 19, 20 years old, and he's going straight downhill at you," LaVine stated.

"We've had plenty of conversations, and we've worked out together and played. But Russ is one of my good friends. My hat's off to him for a hell of a career. He had a lot more to give to basketball too. He could have kept playing, but I'm glad that he walked away on his own terms because not everybody gets to do that," he ended.

Sacramento Kings News: Zach LaVine looks ahead to the 2026-27 NBA season

In the same interview, Zach LaVine said he'll be playing with a chip on his shoulder this upcoming season. He vowed to make the most of his time with the Sacramento Kings, even if it means eventually taking a back seat to make way for the young guys.

"I had a little hand injury, but every year for me, I go into the offseason, I see what I can do better. I see how I can try to help the team and what role or what area I'm gonna be fitting in," LaVine explained . "Obviously, they're going to put you in a role that's best case for you. But I'm super excited."

"It's unfortunate that I had the injury last year, even in the season we had, we started off very well. I started off well. But for standards for myself, I have them extremely high, so I'm looking forward to this year," he continued.

articles.title: WNBA gameday discussion: Can Paige Bueckers, Angel Reese and other stars strengthen their awards candidacies?
articles.summary: Players on the Wings, Dream and Valkyries have the opportunity to add to their WNBA awards resumes.
articles.body:
A three-game WNBA Saturday slate where no game has direct playoff implications serves as a great opportunity for players in contention for end-of-season awards to author a closing argument.

So, here's a look at the primary awards contenders in action on Saturday. In the comments, spill any of your thoughts on the award races.

Phoenix Mercury vs. Dallas Wings (1 p.m. ET, CBS)

A leading candidate for Most Improved Player , Jessica Shepard added to her resume on Thursday, posting her fifth triple-double of the season with 13 points, 11 rebounds and 12 assists in the Dallas Wings' win over the Los Angeles Sparks .

Paige Bueckers , who scored a game-high 19 points, remains in contention for a higher honor: All-WNBA First Team.

As is the case for almost every recognition in this season overflowing record-breaking performances, the All-WNBA field is flooded. Elected to the Second Team as a rookie, Paige has bettered her numbers across the board, scoring 20.4 points per game on 50.8 percent shooting, while dishing 5.8 assists and grabbing 4.1 rebounds.

In various all-in-one advanced metrics, Bueckers ranks in the top 10. She's ninth in Basketball Reference's PER and seventh in both ESPN Analytics' net points and databallr's value plus-minus .

An All-WNBA fixture in recent seasons, it would be a bit surprising if Alyssa Thomas , an All-Star snub , snuck onto a team this year.

AT is still producing at a comparable level, with 14.3 points, 7.7 rebounds and 8.4 assists per game, along with 1.4 steals. But the Phoenix Mercury's disappointing record, likely will leave AT without a fifth-straight All-WNBA nod.

Chicago Sky vs. Atlanta Dream (7 p.m. ET, Prime Video)

In contention for Defense Player of the Year , Angel Reese once again showed the breadth of her game on Thursday, when she dropped a 30-point and 10-rebound double-double to lead the Atlanta Dream's rout of the Connecticut Sun —a performance that outpaced those of her teammates who, like Angel, also should attract All-WNBA attention.

In an otherwise off shooting night, Rhyne Howard made her 129th 3-pointer of the season, establishing a new single-season WNBA record. She finished with 10 points, eight assists, six rebounds and four four steals, a stat line that testifies to how her all-round impact more than compensates for occasional shooting slumps, and explains why Howard has risen to second in ESPN Analytics' MVP ladder .

Allisha Gray also is a top 10 MVP candidate, according ESPN Analytics. On Thursday, she broke one of her own records, scoring the most points in a single season in Dream franchise history with 774 points—and counting.

And after a somewhat slow start to the season, Gray's numbers now mirror those she put up as an All-WNBA First Teamer last season. In fact, she's scoring more (18.4 to 18.9 points per game), shooting more efficiently from the field (45.1 percent to 45.8 percent) and getting to the line more often (5.5 to 5.8 attempts per game). The only knock is her 30 percent 3-point shooting, a significant drop from last season's 38.4 percent.

Jordin Canada also belongs in an end-of-season honor conversation, as she should join Reese and Howard on an All-Defensive team. Canada's 1.9 steals per game rank second in the league, slotting her right between Howard (2.4) and Reese (1.8). That's the most she's averaged since 2023, one of her two All-Defensive seasons with the Seattle Storm .

On the other side, Sydney Taylor already has cemented her All-Rookie nod for the Sky. Otherwise, after getting blown out on Thursday by a Washington Mystics team that (again) owns their first-round draft pick, it will be another "what coulda been" night for Chicago.

Seattle Storm vs. Golden State Valkyries (9 p.m. ET, Prime Video)

The Golden State Valkyries are on a back-to-back in Ballhalla after holding the Portland Fire to 66 points in their Friday night win. It was not only their fifth win in a row, but also the fifth-straight game in which they've held their opponent to under 70 points .

Another lockdown defensive display will add to, and possibly complicate, the award bids for various Valkyries.

For instance, while our Josh Felton boosted Veronica Burton as the Valkyrie who is challenging Reese for Defensive Player of the Year, the organization has promoted Gabby Williams as their preferred DPOY candidate, with Burton joining Williams and Kiah Stokes as All-Defensive nominees.

For Burton, swiping six steals in just 26 minutes on Friday night serves as a nice bit of eye-popping evidence of her defensive impact, raising her average to 1.6 per game for the season. That matches the per-game average of Williams, who was out of action on Friday night.

Janelle Salaün, who likewise did not play after a long FIBA run with France, still can feel secure that the Sixth Player of the Year award will be hers , despite five 3-pointers and 17 points from Kaitlyn Chen . And back-to-back Coach of the Year honors might belong to Natalie Nakase, especially since the No. 1 seed still is a possibility for Golden State.

Since a sixth-straight Valkyrie win is the expectation, might the stage be set for the Storm's award contenders to engineer an upset? Flau'jae Johnson's All-Rookie case is likely signed, sealed and delivered, but Awa Fam's candidacy could use some oomph.

Fam's season high in scoring is 21 points, one of two times she crossed the 20-point barrier. On the rebounding front, she has three games with double-digit boards, topping out at 11 boards.

It would be just one game , but a 22-point and 12-rebound double-double in an upset of Golden State could earn her some extra All-Rookie votes.

articles.title: Joining Forces With The EuroLeague May Be NBA Europe’s Best Path Forward
articles.summary: NBA Europe has been a long time coming, with the league first being announced in early 2025. Europe is dotted with domestic leagues, with the highest level o...
articles.body:
NBA Europe has been a long time coming, with the league first being announced in early 2025. Europe is dotted with domestic leagues, with the highest level of European competition found in the EuroLeague, largely considered the second-best basketball league in the world after the NBA. The EuroLeague has featured current and former NBA players such as Mike James , Kendrick Nunn , and Spencer Dinwiddie .

While the NBA has hosted regular-season international games in several European locations in the past, such as Germany, England, and France, a full-blown league was not remotely a consideration before NBA Europe. Should the two leagues combine?

NBA Europe is expected to be a 16-team league, with 12 permanent teams and four rotational teams that will be decided through a system of promotion and relegation. This will be similar to what is done in European football (soccer). Expected to launch in October 2027, the league will be a joint venture between the NBA and FIBA, the global governing body for basketball.

So, amid talks of the NBA allying with the EuroLeague, and with just a little more than a year remaining until the deadline for the league's inception, is the NBA going to join forces with the EuroLeague?

Making Progress in Discussions With EuroLeague

According to NBA Commissioner Adam Silver, the NBA is 'making progress' in its talks with the EuroLeague on creating a joint league for the continent's premier basketball competition. Additional announcements are expected in the next several weeks.

Initially, NBA Europe was seen as a direct competitor to the EuroLeague, with FIBA partnering with the NBA to bring NBA Europe to fruition. EuroLeague has its own long history with FIBA, as the global basketball body started the league in 1958. However, the two organizations split in the early 2000s following disagreements between FIBA and the teams' owners.

Silver has also noted that there is no particular consensus on whether the two leagues will join forces, but that it is in the best interest of both parties if a 'unified front' is formed in Europe.

Silver also mentioned the timing of NBA Europe's launch. Previous announcements have seen the NBA predicting that NBA Europe will be launched by the fall of 2027 . However, the Commissioner's recent announcements potentially suggest that the NBA may, or would like to, take a little longer to sort everything out before the league finally launches.

According to ESPN , the EuroLeague's team owners are set to meet in Milan on October 5th to discuss their role in NBA Europe. The meeting is to allow EuroLeague clubs to make a decision on whether to accept the NBA's proposal or to continue as an entity separate from NBA Europe.

EuroLeague CEO Chus Bueno has noted that having two high-level basketball leagues on the same continent would fragment the value of both leagues. However, he has no qualms about continuing the EuroLeague as its own separate entity, as any agreement between the two groups would have to work for both sides .

Basketball culture is something that is completely different on the other side of the pond. James, who has played in Europe for nearly a decade and a half, suggested that the NBA would need to attract some 'big teams' in order for the league to be a success. This is because European fans are more team-oriented.

"Because the thing that's different about Europe than the United States is that obviously players have fans and fans like players, but they're really fans of the teams. They grow up with the teams their whole life, and they love them. So you can make NBA Europe and have different teams, but if the big teams aren't over there, the fans are still going to follow the bigger teams and still follow the teams that they've been liking since they were 10. So the whole new league will be nice. Some people will go, but you won't get the passionate fans that they have from the league right now. So I would like for it to combine somehow." — Mike James

NBA Europe plans to have teams in locations such as London, Paris, Madrid, Berlin, Munich, Milan, Rome, Istanbul, Barcelona, Manchester, Lyon, and Athens. The league also appears to have attracted a lot of interest from various ownership groups who have submitted finalized bids. This includes interest from EuroLeague franchises such as FC Barcelona, Real Madrid, LDLC ASVEL (owned and coached by former NBA star Tony Parker ) and Fenerbahce Istanbul.

Over 20 groups have expressed their interest, as all of the bids for franchises came in at $500 million or more, with many bids exceeding $1 billion . Italian basketball club Vanoli Cremona, of which Luka Doncic is a part owner, has notably submitted a bid to bring an NBA Europe to Rome . Former Lakers owners Joey and Jesse Buss have also submitted bids to be a part of NBA Europe through their ownership group, Buss Sports Capital .

Though both leagues play the same sport, there are obvious cultural differences between the fans of the NBA and the EuroLeague. Its former CEO, Paulius Motiejunas , appeared confident in the EuroLeague's future , even with competition from NBA Europe, as the former has been in the market much longer. This is a gap the NBA needs to bridge as it aims for success on the other side of the pond.

While not something that was previously mentioned by either side as a realistic possibility, as talks continue between the NBA and the EuroLeague, it seems more apparent that there are benefits to a partnership for both sides. For the EuroLeague, this will be an opportunity to gain access to a lot more funding and understand the marketing and business side of the sport better, something that stars like James have acknowledged the NBA is better at. For the NBA, the EuroLeague allows them to take advantage of existing teams and fan bases, as well as extensive experience in a completely foreign market. And with time ticking, an NBA partnership with the EuroLeague does not look so unlikely after all.

articles.title: 94 Calls, Jonathan Kuminga's Agent & Wolves GM's Talks Revealed in New Video After Surprise Contract
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves' two-year contract with Jonathan Kuminga was apparently the product of five weeks of extensive negotiating.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves' two-year contract with Jonathan Kuminga was apparently the product of five weeks of extensive negotiating.

Minnesota Timberwolves general manager Matt Lloyd conducted 94 phone calls with Kuminga's agent between July 15 and Aug. 26, he told the Minnesota Star-Tribune 's Michael Rand around the 18:10 mark of Friday's episode of the StribSports Daily Delivery podcast.

5 NBA Stars Who Could Dominate Trade Rumors 🤔

Talks with Kuminga involved Anthony Edwards as well as other members of the team's front office, Lloyd said.

"Anthony was really instrumental in recruiting him to come here," Lloyd said. "We had had several conversations with him, his representatives, from [head coach] Chris Finch, to [president of basketball operations] Tim Connelly, to [basketball operations assistant] Alonzo Gee... everything just kind of came together."

Kuminga agreed to join the Timberwolves on a two-year, $13 million contract with a player option despite reportedly receiving a more lucrative offer from at least one other team.

The Los Angeles Lakers, Chicago Bulls and Portland Trail Blazers also made contract offers to Kuminga, according to ESPN's Shams Charania . The Lakers' offer was a three-year deal worth more than $12 million per year, per Charania.

Kuminga instead decided to accept "a shorter-term deal and an ability to have more control of his future," Charania noted.

The 23-year-old forward averaged 12.2 points, 4.6 rebounds and 2.3 assists in 36 games of a 2025-26 season split between the Golden State Warriors, where he was moved in and out of the rotation before suffering a knee and ankle injury in January, and Atlanta Hawks.

Should he increase his production during a healthier season with potentially more regular playing time in the Wolves's second unit, Kuminga could decide to test free agency again next offseason.

articles.title: Un récord Guinness para abrir la Supercopa Endesa
articles.standfirst: Con 782 participantes el 'Torneo del KO' organizado de forma conjunta por ACB y el Ayuntamiento de Badalona, y patrocinado por Endesa, ha logrado el histórico hito
articles.summary: Con 782 participantes el 'Torneo del KO' organizado de forma conjunta por ACB y el Ayuntamiento de Badalona, y patrocinado por Endesa, ha logrado el histórico hito
articles.body: El 19 de septiembre de 2026 ya queda escrito en la memoria de los aficionados a la Liga Endesa. Esta mañana, 782 personas han completado en la Fan Zone de la Supercopa Endesa Badalona 2026 el Guinness World Record 'The largest game of knockout basketball', el torneo del KO más grande de la historia, patrocinado por Endesa y organizado conjuntamente por la acb y el Ayuntamiento de Badalona. Con esta cifra se supera el anterior récord, en poder de la Universidad de Duke con 711 participantes, quien a su vez se lo había arrebatado a los Dallas Mavericks, que lo habían fijado en 705. La adjudicadora de Guinness World Records, Anouk de Timary, presente en la Fan Zone para certificar oficialmente la marca, ha sido la encargada de entregar a la acb la placa que acredita el récord conseguido. Josep Perich (dorsal 298) se ha proclamado ganador del reto, haciéndose con el tan deseado abono doble con alojamiento para la Copa del Rey de Valencia 2026. Antonio Martín, presidente de la acb; Xavier García Albiol, Alcalde de Badalona; Enric Brazís, director de Endesa en Cataluña y Juanan Morales, presidente del ASISA Joventut, participaron en el acto inicial del reto, que también contó con la presencia de Anna Cruz, Jordi Villacampa, Albert Ventura y Toñín Llorente. De esta forma, la Liga Endesa 2026-27 arranca la temporada por todo lo alto, reuniendo esta mañana a cientos de amantes del baloncesto en Badalona. ¡Qué mejor manera de empezar la temporada!

articles.summary: El club catalán confirma la confianza en el técnico gallego firmándole por una temporada más
articles.body: El entrenador Moncho Fernández y el FIATC Girona han llegado a un acuerdo para ampliar la vinculación del técnico un año más, hasta junio de 2028, según ha informado el club catalán este sábado, a una semana del inicio de la Liga Endesa. El comunicado del Girona destaca que su renovación llega tras el "hito histórico" de la primera clasificación para competiciones europeas y reitera la "confianza" en el proyecto de Moncho. El técnico gallego recaló en Fontajau en diciembre de 2024 con el reto de salvar a un equipo que era colista con dos victorias en once jornadas y ya suma 57 partidos al mando del Girona. La temporada pasada el equipo consiguió su mejor posición (12º) y su récord de victorias (14) en la Liga Endesa y ahora se prepara para el debut en la Copa de la Europa de la FIBA. "Se ha consolidado como una pieza fundamental de la nave deportiva del club. Bajo su dirección, el club ha firmado la mejor trayectoria de su recorrido reciente", reivindica el comunicado. El texto añade que Moncho continuará dirigiendo al equipo catalán con el objetivo de "consolidar al club en la Liga Endesa y afrontar con ambición el nuevo reto europeo". En el mismo sentido, el director deportivo, Fernando San Emeterio, ha asegurado en unas declaraciones distribuidas por el propio Girona da "mucha tranquilidad saber que estará como mínimo dos años más con nosotros, para continuar construyendo juntos". Moncho, nacido hace 57 años en Santiago de Compostela, suma 501 partidos en 17 temporadas en la ACB.

articles.title: El Fenerbahce se consuela más que el Dubái en el partido por el tercer puesto
articles.standfirst: Los turcos acaban su participación en Abu Dabi con mejores sensaciones
articles.summary: Los turcos acaban su participación en Abu Dabi con mejores sensaciones
articles.body: Si hay un partido en la SuperCup que sí representa claramente la pretemporada, es la lucha por el tercer y cuarto puesto. Con nada en juego, Fenerbahce y Dubai Basketball tardaron mucho más que en las semifinales en entran en calor, y eso que estamos en Abu Dabi, donde por la noche puede hacer tranquilamente 37 o 38 grados. Pero tras perder el billete a la final, sólo quedaba el orgullo de no acabar la competición con un 0-2 y con las mejores sensaciones posibles. Por eso el Fenerbahce se va mejor de Abu Dabi que el Dubai. Compitió hasta el final con el Olympiacos y ganó el choque de consolación, 85-77, después de ver cómo su rival le remontaba y amenazaba con ganarle hasta que se quedó sin fuerzas. El equipo turco tuvo la primera gran ventaja con un 42-33 a 1:51 para el final del segundo cuarto. Cuando se habían disputado cuatro minutos del tercer acto, esa diferencia se había esfumado (51-51) y poco después era el Dubái el equipo que iba por delante merced a un triples de Bertans. El equipo de Xavi Pasucal parecía más entero con la llegada del último cuarto y tuvo su máxima a 8:37 para el final, 64-70. Fue cuando los locales empezaron a notar más haber jugado más tarde y haber gastado más energías en su partido contra el Madrid por culpa de la prórroga. Un 20-5 dejaba el marcador muy encarrilado para el Fenerbahce, 84-75, que sólo tuvo que esperar a que el partido acabara para llevarse el triunfo. Partido especialmente brillante de Talen Horton-Tucker, 22 puntos, ayudado por Baldwin, 11 y dos triples en pleno parcial ganador de su equipo, y Forrest, también 11. En el Dubái, que en cinco días recibe al Madrid en el primer partido de la Liga regular, Okobo y Bertans alcanzaron los 14, y Kabengele firmó 9.

articles.title: Brandon Clarke to Be Honored by Grizzlies with Jersey Patch Following Death
articles.summary: The Memphis Grizzlies announced Saturday that they will honor late forward Brandon Clarke during their 2026-27 NBA regular-season home opener and throughout the upcoming campaign.
articles.body:
The Memphis Grizzlies announced Saturday that they will honor late forward Brandon Clarke during their 2026-27 NBA regular-season home opener and throughout the upcoming campaign.

The Grizzlies said that they will have a pre-game tribute and moment of silence for Clarke prior to their opening night game against the Utah Jazz on Oct. 21, and they will also wear a "BC" patch on their jerseys for the entirety of the 2026-27 season:

Clarke, who played seven seasons for the Grizzlies from 2019 to 2026, died in May at the age of 29.

In August, the Los Angeles County medical examiner's office (h/t ESPN's Tom Schad ) announced that Clarke died from an accidental drug overdose.

Born in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, Clarke played collegiately at Gonzaga before getting selected 21st overall in the 2019 NBA draft.

Clarke spent his entire career in Memphis, starting 50 of the 309 regular season games he appeared in. He averaged 10.2 points, 5.5 rebounds and 1.3 assists, while shooting 60.5 percent from the field.

With averages of 12.1 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game, Clarke finished fourth in NBA Rookie of the Year voting in 2020, and he was named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team.

Clarke was at his best during the Grizzlies' first-round playoff series win over the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2022, averaging 16.5 points, 9.0 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.0 block over the course of the six-game series.

Clarke was limited to six games in 2023-24 due to a torn Achilles and two games last season because of knee and calf ailments.

Clarke is the Grizzlies' all-time leader in career field-goal percentage, and he ranks 10th in team history with 246 blocks.

articles.summary: En su regreso al Asisa Joventut el veterano base comanda el triunfo ante un Kosner Baskonia con muchas lagunas
articles.body: El Asisa Joventut, reforzado por su condición de anfitrión, sometió al Kosner Baskonia (96-84) y se clasificó para la final de la Supercopa. En un partido en el que entre ambos equipos presentaban 11 caras nuevas, fue un viejo conocido de la Liga Endesa, Nico Laprovittola, quien desequilibró la balanza en su regreso a la Penya con un recital en la dirección. El base argentino de 36 años dominó el partido a su antojo con una dirección formidable (10 asistencias) y una contribución anotadora fantástica con 27 puntos (3/7 t2, 5/10 t3 y 6/9 tl) en 27 minutos, para un total de 28 créditos de valoración. Complementaron su labor con los locales el icónico Ricky Rubio (13+6+3 en 21 minutos), Sulejmanovic (12+6) y Reyes (10+5). El irregular Baskonia plantó cara hasta el tercer cuarto gracias, principalmente, a la producción de Kobi Simmons (19+2+6), AJ Lawson (16+3), a los que ayudaron puntualmente Spagnolo (10+8+4), Duarte (10+3) y DJ Stewart (11+4+2). Pero echaron de menos a Markus Howard (0 puntos en 17 minutos), antiguo líder de este equipo que se ha convertido en una rémora, y pagaron caro su nefasto acierto desde el tiro libre (17/31), un 55% de eficacia impropia de un equipo profesional. Ricky Rubio, como era de esperar, se apoderó del ritmo del partido desde el salto inicial para aguantar las embestidas del Baskonia con un AJ Lawson muy incisivo. Los verdinegros no levantaron el pie del acelerador cuando se sentó su icono, reemplazado por un Laprovittola que en su retorno a la Penya asumió la responsabilidad ofensiva con nueve puntos para nivelar el choque en el primer acto (20-23) con muchos errores de ambos equipos desde el triple. Empezaron mejor el segundo cuarto los baskonistascon un Kobi Simmons muy enchufado que comandó la primera escapada seria de su equipo tras una técnica por protestar a Dani Miret (23-31, min 14). Volvió a cancha Laprovittola para desatascar el ataque de su equipo y lo logró con ayuda de Ndiaye (30-32). Tras un intercambio de 'pedradas' desde el triple acertaron por fin Spagnolo y Ndiaye, y Ricky irrumpió con un 2+1 a aro pasado marca de la casa para mantener la igualdad al descanso (38-41, min 20). En la reanudación AJ Lawson, Simmons y Sedekerskis pusieron el contrapunto a las embestidas de Ellis y Ndiaye. (49-50). Entonces fue Laprovittola quien se adueñó del choque para liderar un parcial de 19-7 con su dirección y con sus puntos, bien complementado por Cheatham y Sulejmanovic (68-57, min 30). El Baskonia no veía aro desde el triple... ni desde el tiro libre (14/25). Así era muy difícil competir. Ellis y Laprovittola pusieron la máxima para la Penya (77-64, min 34). Pero el Baskonia no se rindió y entre AJ Lawson, Simmons y Duarte se metió en el partido (78-71). Enfriaron su reacción los verdinegros conun triple de Laprovittola y una canasta de Sulejmanovic (85-71, min 36). Ocho puntos seguidos de DJ Stewart y un triple de Kurucs dieron el último aliento a los vitorianos (87-82), pero Laprovittola, el MVP del partido, abrochó el triunfo con dos asistencias a Birgander (96-84).

articles.title: Kevin Love Trolls Kyle Lowry Over 'LeBronto' in Video from Block Party Celebration for Raptors Icon
articles.summary: Kevin Love had some fun with his former rival-turned-teammate Kyle Lowry at the Lowry's block party celebration in Maple Leaf Square on Saturday.
articles.body:
Kevin Love had some fun with his former rival-turned-teammate Kyle Lowry at the Lowry's block party celebration in Maple Leaf Square on Saturday.

During the event celebrating Lowry's NBA career, Love showed up to joke that he was surprised about all the pageantry for Lowry because he thought they were in "LeBronto."

5 NBA Stars Who Could Dominate Trade Rumors 🤔

The joke is a reference to the mid-2010s rivalry between the Toronto Raptors and Cleveland Cavaliers. Thos teams met in the playoffs three consecutive years from 2016 to 2018, with LeBron James and the Cavs winning all three matchups.

Two of them ended in four-game sweeps, leading to ESPN announcer Mark Jones saying in Game 2 of the 2018 Eastern Conference semifinals that "we'll be back to LeBronto for the fourth quarter" as the network was going to commercial.

Lowry and the Raptors did eventually get their NBA championship during the 2018-19 season with Kawhi Leonard leading them past the Golden State Warriors.

A 20-year NBA veteran, Lowry retired in July by signing a one-day contract with Toronto where he played nine seasons. The Raptors held a block party on Saturday to celebrate his career and interact with fans.

The Raptors will retire Lowry's No. 7 jersey during a game against James and the Philadelphia 76ers on Jan. 10.

articles.title: WNBA Playoff Bracket 2026 and Seeding Scenarios for Updated Picture
articles.summary: Although the eight 2026 WNBA playoff teams were already decided entering play on Saturday, there was still plenty of room for movement in terms of seeding.
articles.body:
Although the eight 2026 WNBA playoff teams were already decided entering play on Saturday, there was still plenty of room for movement in terms of seeding.

Three playoff teams were set to be in action Saturday with the Dallas Wings hosting the Phoenix Mercury, the Atlanta Dream hosting the Chicago Sky and the Golden State Valkyries hosting the Seattle Storm.

Here is a look at where the top eight teams in the WNBA currently sit in the standings amid Saturday's slate of games, as well as a snapshot of what the first-round playoff matchups would be if the season ended today.

2. Golden State Valkyries: 30-11 (1.0 GB)

1. Minnesota Lynx vs. 8. Washington Mystics

2. Golden State Valkyries vs. 7. New York Liberty

Led by superstar guard Paige Bueckers, the Wings jumped from the No. 8 seed to the No. 6 seed on Saturday, at least temporarily.

Dallas began the day in a three-way tie with the New York Liberty and Washington Mystics at 25-16. By beating the Mercury 87-82, the Wings are now a half-game ahead of New York and Washington at 26-16.

Bueckers was excellent and efficient as usual on Saturday, scoring a game-high 26 points on 10-of-19 shooting to go along with five assists, four rebounds and three steals.

When play started on Saturday, Dallas was lined up for a first-round playoff matchup against the top-seeded Lynx, but it would now take on the No. 3 Las Vegas Aces if the season ended today.

Led by four-time WNBA MVP A'ja Wilson, the Aces are the reigning WNBA champions, and they have won three of the past four titles.

It is far from guaranteed that the Wings and Aces will meet in the first round, though, as the Wings still have two regular-season games remaining, while the Liberty and Mystics have three each.

With a win in their game against the Sky at 7 p.m. ET, the Dream will remain fourth in the standings, but they will move within a half-game of the third-place Aces.

However, should Atlanta lose to Chicago, it will drop into fifth place, a half-game behind the Indiana Fever.

In the 9 p.m. ET game, the Valkyries can cut the Minnesota Lynx's lead for the No. 1 seed from one game to a half-game with a victory over the Storm.

Should Golden State lose to last-place Seattle, it will remain in second, 1.5 games behind the Lynx and 1.5 games ahead of the Aces.

articles.title: Wheelchair basketball: Great Britain men beat Germany to win World Championship bronze
articles.summary: Great Britain men's team win bronze at the Wheelchair Basketball World Championships by defeating Germany, but GB women lose out in third-place play-off.
articles.body:
Great Britain men's team won bronze at the Wheelchair Basketball World Championships by defeating Germany 67-56 in the third-place play-off.

After conceding an early lead in Ottawa, GB scored twice in less than a minute and stayed in front from then on, with Gregg Warburton leading his side's scoring with 20 points.

The outcome means Britain's men have won a medal at three consecutive World Championships after taking gold and silver at the 2018 and 2022 editions.

GB women missed out on a medal as they lost 63-50 to the Netherlands in their third-place match.

Britain, captained by Sophie Carrigill, trailed after two periods but levelled the scoring at 44-44 heading into the final quarter of the match.

The Netherlands, champions in 2018 and 2022, then stepped it up and dominated the closing quarter 19-6 to secure another medal.

Fourth place is still a big improvement for GB women, who finished ninth at the 2022 edition of the tournament.

articles.title: El nuevo Madrid ya sabe ganar finales: ¡supercampeón de Europa!
articles.standfirst: Derrota al Olympiacos en un partido que controló casi en todo momento
articles.summary: Derrota al Olympiacos en un partido que controló casi en todo momento
articles.body: El Real Madrid se llevó el primer título de la temporada, el primero de Pedro Marínez a los mandos y el primero después de un año en blanco. Ganó al Olympiacos, 89-93, en un partido que supo gestionar como si no hubiera tenido hasta siete novedades en la pretemporada. Si Pedro Martínez saca conclusiones de esta SuperCup, serán casi todas positivas. Sabedor del potencial de su rival, vigente campeón y reforzado durante la pretemporada, el Madrid cogió el partido por la solapa. No quería dejarlo escapar. De esa forma estableció las primeras ventajas. El Olympiacos tuvo la primera (2-0), pero el Madrid se adueñó de inmediato del partido para un parcial de 0-9 y poner el 12-22 en el marcador. Ese parcial llegó con tres triples seguidos. Pedro Martínez quería más tiros desde el arco y los tuvo. Al final del primer tiempo los blancos llevaban los mismos tiros de dos (16) que de tres. Esa será una constante en el juego del Madrid. Otra, los numerosos cambios que el técnico introduce en el partido. A 1:28 para el final del primer cuarto, que ganó el Madrid, 15-24, Martínez ya había metido en pista a sus 12 jugadores, incluso con cambios de cinco en cinco. Bartzokas, como ejemplo, aún tenía cinco jugadores en su banquillo que no se habían estrenado. Otra de las señas del Madrid será el contraataque y el juego a toda velocidad. Pero eso trae como problemas las pérdidas. Al final del primer cuarto había extraviado 7 balones, al descanso eran 13. El Madrid siguió mandando en el segundo acto con ventajas que oscilaban en la decena (15-25, 27-37 o 30-40), a pesar del intento de remontada del Olympiacos que se produjo gracias a las muchas faltas personales que los árbitros señalaron a los blancos. Tavares, por ejemplo, se fue al banco a 4:06 con tres. Un gran triple de Jantunen y un canastón de Corey Joseph dejaron el marcador en 43-47 cuando el reloj mandó a los jugadores al vestuario. Salió mejor el Olympiacos en la reanudación y en poco tiempo ya volvía a mandar en el partido: 50-47. Cierta precipitación, con varias pérdidas dio la iniciativa a los griegos que llegaron a tener varias veces cinco puntos de máxima (61-56, 63-58). El Madrid seguía lanzando triples. De sus seis primeros tiros en el tercer cuarto, cinco fueron desde el arco. Deck, por ejemplo, clavó dos seguidos. En el peor momento del Madrid apareció Maledon para forzar varias entradas con éxito. Anotó ocho de sus 10 puntos en ese periodo. Pero los problemas de los blancos estaban en las faltas. Los árbitros pitaron desequilibrado 11/21 a cuatro minutos del final. En ese momento, Luwawu-Cabarrot y Okeke ya estaban con cuatro. Un triple de Abalde devolvió la ventaja al Madrid (68-69), que amplió hasta el 70-75. Los blancos se complicaron la vida en los últimos segundos con una falta de Jantunen a Montero y una técnica a Pedro Martínez que no fue peor porque el dominicano falló el segundo libre y el tiro de su propio rebote (72-75). El arranque de cuarto periodo del Madrid fue fabuloso: un 0-7 para devolver los 10 al marcador con un certero triple de Luwawu-Cabarrot, que volvió a pista con sus cuatro faltas. El Madrid crecía en el partido por encima del Olympiacos. Apareció Vezenkov para anotar cinco puntos seguidos, y con 83-89, Tavares perdió un balón cuando todo indicaba que iba a anotar, castigado con el triple de Fournier (86-89 a 2:22). Dos libres de Campazzo, dieron un respiro a los blancos que, de nuevo se volvieron a meter en un lío. Una pérdida de Pradilla en una jugada que no debió pasar acabó con otro triple de Fournier, 'on fire' en el final. El Olympiacos se colocaba a una sola canasta (89-91) a 1:15. Montero le devolvió la posesión al Madrid porque pisó la línea lateral. El fallo en el triple de Pradilla lo recuperó Luwawu-Cabarrot en un rebote salvador que Feliz convirtió en la canasta que sellaba el triunfo del Madrid en la primera final de la temporada: 89-93. Partido muy coral en el aspecto anotador y en el protagonismo de los jugadores del Madrid. Luwawu-Cabarrot fue el mejor con 12, Pradilla, Jantunen y Feliz firmaron 11 cada uno y Maledon hizo 10. Tavares se quedó en 6, pero cogió 7 rebotes, y su presencia al final fue decisiva para contener al Olympiacos. Por eso se llevó el MVP de la final. Vezenkov al final se fue con 22 puntos, Fournier con 14 y Hall con 13.

articles.title: Tavares, un MVP gigante
articles.standfirst: El pívot fue elegido como mejor jugador de la SuperCup
articles.summary: El pívot fue elegido como mejor jugador de la SuperCup
articles.body: Edy Tavares se llevó el premio MVP de la SuperCup. No fue el jugador que más puntos anotó en la final ante el Olympiacos, pero sí el jugador más determinante en los dos aros. A pesar de estar lastrado por las faltas personales, el pívot madridista se protegió para poder estar en pista en el tramo decisivo del partido donde varias acciones suyas, incluso condicionando algunos tiros o penetraciones, resultaron fundamentales. El gigante del Madrid acabó con seis puntos, sin fallo en el tiro, siete rebotes y siete de valoración en los 20 minutos que estuvo en pista. De nuevo su juego impulsó al Madrid, y eso que la dinámica de lanzar de tres mucho y rápido hará que por sus manos pasen menos balones que antes. Aún así, sigue siendo el jugador más determinante en la pintura en Europa. Este es el cuarto MVP que gana Tavares en una fase final con el Real Madrid tras los logrados en la Final Four de la Euroliga en 2023, la final de la Liga Endesa en 2022 y la Supercopa de España también de 2022. A pesar del nuevo rumbo que el equipo está tomando con el juego que quiere imponer Pedro Martínez, Tavares sigue siendo imprescindible. "Estoy muy feliz por ganar la primera SuperCup. Es importante porque quiere decir que hemos hechos las cosas bien aunque queda mucho por mejorar. Y estoy feliz por ganar con Pedro (Martínez) porque es alguien que creyó en mí cuando nadie lo hacía", dijo Tavares ante la prensa una vez acabado el partido. "El equipo ha hecho un buen trabajo. Ha sido un partido muy ajustado y cuando el equipo gana todo el mundo gana. Este premio me ha tocado a mí, pero le podía haber tocado a cualquiera".

articles.title: Paige Bueckers' highlight-reel 3s fuel 20-point first half as Wings beat Mercury, nab franchise-record 26th win
articles.summary: Dallas has won six straight games and is jockeying for improved playoff seeding amid its turnaround season.
articles.body:
Paige Bueckers hit a pair of head-turning, step-back 3-pointers on Saturday against the Phoenix Mercury , one in the first half and another in the second half that helped her Dallas Wings secure an 87-82 victory over the Phoenix Mercury.

In between, the two-time All-Star guard knocked down a triple while drawing a foul right before intermission , a sequence that sent the College Park Center crowd into a frenzy.

With the Wings playing their final regular-season game in the Arlington arena ahead of their 2027 move to Dallas' American Airlines Center, Bueckers put on a show. She finished with 26 points on 10-of-19 shooting to go along with her 5 assists, 4 rebounds and 3 steals.

Despite a furious fight from the Mercury (15-27) — in which Alyssa Thomas posted her WNBA-leading 23rd career triple-double (19 points, 11 assists and 10 rebounds) — the Wings (26-16) extended their six-game win streak. In the process, they logged their 26th victory of 2026, setting the franchise single-season wins record a year removed from winning 10 games.

Bueckers pocketed 20 of her points in the opening half. Over the first two quarters, she converted four of her five 3-point attempts.

She was a big part of the Wings soaring toward a 37-point second quarter. They capitalized off Mercury turnovers and ran the break.

In the second half, however, Phoenix increased attention on Bueckers, who was held scoreless throughout the third quarter. Luckily for Dallas, she had plenty of help, even in the backcourt, where Arike Ogunbowale had her turn in the spotlight.

Ogunbowale, a four-time All-Star, clocked out with 22 points and six assists.

Phoenix hung around, though, and not just because of Thomas. The Mercury also got 16 points from Natasha Mack and, most notably, a team-high 21 points from second-year guard Lexi Held .

For reference, Held came in averaging a smidge over five points. She brought swagger on the road, matching Bueckers' efforts from beyond the arc. Held went 4 of 5 from 3-point land and at one point in the final frame gave the Dallas bench a look after drilling a corner 3.

With less than two and a half minutes to go, Sami Whitcomb cashed in from long range, too, pulling the Mercury within one point.

She and Dallas gripped to that slightly cushioned lead from there on out, moving up to sixth in the W's standings.

articles.title: El Madrid estrena palmarés: así fueron sus otras 'primeras veces'
articles.standfirst: No es la primera vez en la historia que los blancos ganan el primer título de una competición
articles.summary: No es la primera vez en la historia que los blancos ganan el primer título de una competición
articles.body: Chus Bueno dijo en la previa de la SuperCup que esta de Abu Dabi no era una edición más, era la primera, esa que todos quieren ganar. Y es cierto, cuando una competición nace, el equipo que gana su primera edición es único. Otros podrán ganar las siguientes pero, la primera sólo la puede ganar uno. El Madrid estrenó el palmarés de la SuperCup de la Euroliga. Si sopesamos pros y contras de esta competición, tiene toda la pinta de que vaya a tener una vida muy larga. Es un torneo que finaliza la preparación de los equipos y les lanza al arranque de la temporada pero, como dijo Bartzokas, es una Final Four a mitad de septiembre. Una novedosa idea que se salda con la palabra éxito en Abu Dabi. El Madrid será en la historia de este torneo el primer campeón. Eso ya no lo mueve nadie. Campazzo estaba ilusionado con eso: "Siempre que ganas el primer título de una competición es muy especial". Pero, ¿cuántas veces ha tenido esa misma sensación el Madrid a lo largo de su historia? La SuperCup es su título 101 en las vitrinas de los blancos en la sección de baloncesto. Es el equipo más laureado de todos los tiempos y, además de la SuperCup, ha inaugurado otros palmarés. El primero fue el de la Liga española. Ha pesar de que el Barça ganó en 1946-47, ese título nunca fue reconocido por la federación española, organizadora hasta 1984. Aquella, según la historia, fue una especie de prueba y no hubo más competición hasta 1956-57, la primera según la federación, que sí ganó el Madrid. Por si acaso, los blancos también ganaron la primera edición que organizó la ACB, en 1983-84, en un final precisamente ante el Barcelona. Los blancos también ganaron la primera Supercopa de España, ahora Supercopa Endesa. Fue en 1984, entonces organizada por la ACEB en una final ante el Zaragoza. Se jugaron cuatro ediciones y después desapareció del calendario para volver en 2004, que también ganó el Madrid. Era la quinta edición y ya estaba organizada por la ACB. Otro título que inauguró el Madrid es la Copa Latina. Se jugaron sólo dos ediciones, 1952-53 y 1965-66 la primera la ganó el Madrid y la segunda el Olimpia de Milán. No hubo más. En el resto de competiciones ganadas por el Madrid, los blancos tuvieron que esperar a ganar su primer título. En la Copa Intercontinental el Corinthians estrenó el palmarés y el Madrid no ganó hasta 1976, la décima edición. En la Copa de Europa el ASK Riga de Letonia se llevó el estreno y los blancos no ganaron hasta 1963-64. La ULEB que ganaron en 2004 (y 2007) la había ganado antes el Valencia (2003), la Recopa o Copa Saporta la ganó cuatro veces pero tardó varios años en estrenarse y en la Copa de España o Copa del Rey tuvo que esperar 15 ediciones (1951, como Copa del Generalísimo) para levantarla. Eso sí, ganó la edición 41 que era la primera vez que se denominaba Copa del Rey y luego la 48 que por primera vez fue Copa del Rey ACB.

articles.title: El Barça luchará por romper su sequía de tres años sin títulos
articles.standfirst: Punter liquida al Valencia Basket con un tiro libre a falta de dos segundos y los azulgranas se medirán a la Penya en la final de la Supercopa Endesa
articles.summary: Punter liquida al Valencia Basket con un tiro libre a falta de dos segundos y los azulgranas se medirán a la Penya en la final de la Supercopa Endesa
articles.body: El duelo entre equipos reconstruidos lo resolvió uno de los que ya estaban: Kevin Punter. El escolta dio el triunfo al Barcelona con un tiro libre a falta de dos segundos y metió a los suyos en la final de la Supercopa Endesa. Los azulgranas, que se medirán este domingo al anfitrión Asisa Joventut (19.00 horas), tendrán la oportunidad de acabar con esa terrible racha de tres temporadas sin sumar un título. La reedición de la última final de la Liga Endesa tuvo poco que ver con aquello por todas las caras nuevas que había: 20 fichajes entre los dos equipos. Eso, a estas alturas de temporada, equivale a falta de fluidez y a muchos detalles por pulir. Pero se vio a lo que quieren jugar los dos equipos. El Valencia Basket, con Xavi Albert en lugar de Pedro Martínez en el banquillo, a correr, como en la era anterior. Pero el Barça de Aleksander Sekulic no le dejó hacerlo, tirando de músculo y dominando el rebote. Serán dos de sus señas de identidad. Los azulgranas impusieron su físico durante buena parte de un partido interminable por culpa de las revisiones arbitrales. Nkamhoua (10+12) y Nebo (11+8) mandaron en la zona. Al menos hasta que el segundo estrenó las nuevas normas y fue expulsado por dos flagrantes a falta de nueve minutos. Lucieron también Justin Robinson, eléctrico en la dirección y acertado de cara al aro (17), y Joel Parra, chico para todo (12). A los taronjas, en los que aún no debutó Nikola Mirotic, les sostuvieron Kameron Taylor (23) y el liderazgo de TJ Shorts (17), que consiguió 11 de sus 29 créditos de valoración en el último periodo. Apoyado en su aplastante dominio del rebote (37-51) y en acciones individuales, el Barça llegó a tener 10 puntos de renta (45-55 y 48-58), pero no supo despegarse, en parte, por la gran cantidad de balones que perdió: 21. Los valencianos se agarraban al partido sumando desde el tiro libre, aunque se dejaban alguno en cada viaje (59-62). La expulsión de Nebo, después de una segunda flagrante por un roce con Brooks, no afectó mucho al Barça, que se intentaba escapar con triples de Robinson y Tyrese Martin (72-79). Shorts tiró de los taronjas, que fallaron varios triples para empatar. Lo hicieron por fin a falta de 35 segundos con tres tiros libres de Taylor (84-84). Después, sendos canastones de Robinson y Shorts para volver a igualar. El base del Barça, en el último ataque, casi se come el balón. Le dio la patata caliente a Punter, que recibió falta de Taylor con dos segundos por jugar. El capitán azulgrana metió el primer tiro libre y falló el segundo. Dylan Osetkowski atrapó el rebote y, desde su propio aro, casi emboca un triple milagroso. El Barça estaba en la final y tratará de romper su pésima racha sin títulos.

articles.title: Pedro Martínez: "Espero que este título nos dé energía para seguir trabajando"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Madrid habla de la victoria de su equipo ante el Olympiacos
articles.summary: El técnico del Madrid habla de la victoria de su equipo ante el Olympiacos
articles.body: Lo de Pedro Masrtínez ha sido llegar y besar el santo. El Real Madrid estuvo toda la pasada temporada persiguiendo títulos y no ganó ninguno. Fue la primera temporada en blanco en muchos años y había preocupación. En apenas unos meses al frente, Pedro Martínez ya ha hecho que la presente no vaya a ser de nuevo una campaña vacía. Obviamente no es el título que el club tiene como objetivo, pero el técnico catalán ha demostrado que lleva el equipo por el camino que él esperaba. Tras la victoria, y una buena celebración en el vestuario, Pedro Martínez salió a dar cuentas a la sala de prensa. Y se le vio satisfecho: "En esta competición fuimos cuatro los mejores equipos de Europa. Para nosotros es muy importante, porque creo que trabajamos duro en la pretemporada, con muchos nuevos jugadores, y para mí es genial ver que tienen una gran mentalidad y creen en el día a día de lo que hicimos en esta pretemporada. Y espero que nos dé confianza para seguir en el camino, con la mentalidad para mejorar y trabajar juntos". El Madrid corta de esta forma la sequía de títulos que ha durado una temporada: "Hablé con nuestro presidente, Florentino Pérez, y estaba muy feliz después de una temporada difícil. Es genial para nosotros, individualmente y como equipo. Y nos da, espero, más energía para seguir trabajando, porque acabamos la pretemporada hace unos días, pero tenemos que mejorar. Como Olimpiakos, como todos los equipos que participaron en esta competición importante, estamos empezando, y tenemos que saber que esto no es suficiente. Necesitamos mejorar. Por ejemplo, hoy no jugamos bien el último cuarto. Necesitamos tener un mejor conocimiento entre los entrenadores y los jugadores para jugar mejor, porque en el futuro otros equipos van a mejorar y tenemos que hacer lo mismo". Martínez se refirió también a las conclusiones que le deja la SuperCup: "Nosotros consideramos que la competición oficial empezó en este torneo, y la pretemporada celebramos que la habíamos acabado antes de viajar aquí. Lo que estoy es contento de la mentalidad que están teniendo los jugadores en el día a día, que están creyendo en lo que hacemos, que están jugando con muchísimo esfuerzo, que se llevan muy bien entre ellos, creo que tienen una muy buena química interna, por lo que veo cuando estamos en el hotel o antes de los entrenamientos y después de los entrenamientos. Eso me hace pensar que con trabajo vamos a seguir mejorando. Yo creo que es un buen inicio para la confianza. Mañana vamos a descansar, pero el lunes tenemos que entrenar y tenemos que hacer el mejor entrenamiento posible, después de ganar, o igual si hubiéramos perdido. Esto está muy bien, ahora estamos celebrando el presente, pero debemos ser conscientes de que llevamos poco tiempo juntos y que tenemos que mejorar". Finalmente, el técnico habló de los roles importantes repartidos en su equipo y del MVP a Tavares: "Tenemos una plantilla muy larga y todos los jugadores son importantes. Los que han jugado hoy, los que jugaron el otro día, los necesitamos a todos para una temporada muy exigente, en la cual vamos a jugar seguro más de 90 partidos y necesitamos que estén todos con confianza y sintiéndose importantes. Unos días serán unos y otros días serán otros. Yo estoy contento porque me parece muy merecido el MVP de Tavares, porque no todo son estadísticas y lo que él nos ha ayudado condicionando el juego, trabajando, en defensa, corriendo contraataque, ha tenido un impacto brutal. Pero lo importante es que estamos creando un poco esa mentalidad y esa cultura de que el equipo está por encima de todos".
