articles.title: How likely is it that the Nets will be better than expected?
articles.summary: The Brooklyn Nets are expected by many around the NBA to be one of the worst teams in the league this year, but how likely are they to beat the odds?
articles.body:
The Brooklyn Nets came into the 2026 NBA offseason with the goal of improving the team as much as possible following a 2025-26 season in which they finished with a lowly 20-62 record. Brooklyn's main move of the summer was trading for former Minnesota Timberwolves forward Julius Randle , but how likely is it for them to beat the odds this upcoming season?

"If there is one team in the NBA that looks like someone just threw a bunch of players that don't fit together on a roster for no reason whatsoever, it's the Brooklyn Nets ," Brett Siegel wrote on the Nets for ClutchPoints. Siegel put together a tier list of all 30 NBA teams into seven tiers with the Nets making it into the category of the team seemingly destined for the relegation zone.

"Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. trying to play off one another is not a recipe for success, and the Nets are still putting a lot of faith in their recent first-round picks to pan out," Siegel continued. " Egor Demin and Mikel Brown Jr. offer small bright spots for Brooklyn, but the vast majority of this roster won't make it past February's trade deadline."

While the partnership between forwards Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle still needs some time to develop, Siegel makes a good point in that the Nets have plenty invested in the five first-round picks from the 2025 NBA Draft. Guard Egor Demin is likely to start in the backcourt for head coach Jordi Fernandez, but the other four will likely be coming off the bench with guard Nolan Traore and forward Danny Wolf primed to be in the rotation.

The Nets are projected by many to win somewhere between 20 games and 30 games given that the team still needs to add more talent to the roster before it's ready to compete for the playoffs. Porter and Randle are slated to be the leaders of the team and while anything can happen between now and the February trade deadline, the Nets have the goal of being better than what most are expecting from them.

articles.title: Angel Reese makes WNBA history (again!) with 500 rebounds in a season
articles.summary: Angel Reese is in a league of her own after grabbing her 500th rebound this WNBA season.
articles.body:
COLLEGE PARK, GA ― Angel Reese 's record-breaking WNBA season continues with another historic feat.

On Saturday, Reese became the first player in league history to secure 500 rebounds in a single season. The Dream forward had 495 rebounds ahead of a matchup against Chicago , but was on a mission from the opening tip.

Reese's record-sealing rebound came in the 1:50 minute of the second quarter. Reese appeared to cause a deflection on a ball and then grabbed a defensive rebound, giving her 500 total boards this season.

Setting records is not new to Reese. She's been achieving them throughout the 2026 season. On Sunday, Aug. 30, Reese recorded her 29th double-double of the season in the Atlanta Dream 's 89-81 win over the Minnesota Lynx . She worked her way up to 13 points and grabbed 10 rebounds at the 5:40 mark of the fourth quarter, setting a new WNBA single-season double-doubles record . Alyssa Thomas previously held the record (28), which she set in 2023 during a 40-game regular season.

Barbie's Dream House came to Atlanta for Angel Reese, WNBA collab

On Monday, Aug. 24, during the Dream's 78-71 win over the Los Angeles Sparks , Reese set a WNBA single-game record with 26 total rebounds (18 defensive and eight offensive boards). The same day, Reese also set a new single-season rebounding record with 458 total rebounds. Reese surpassed the previous mark of 451 rebounds set by Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson in 2024.

The aforementioned milestones are not the only ones Reese has achieved in 2026. She reached 900 career rebounds in only 71 games on May 29, the fastest to that mark in WNBA history. She scored the 1,000th point of her WNBA career in the Dream's 91-75 win over Connecticut on June 2.

"Anything that goes up is mine," Reese said on Aug. 24. "I want to be one of (the best) when I walk away from the game. So just being able to … be consistent every night is something I'm looking forward to doing."

Reese, who is fresh off winning gold with Team USA at the FIBA World Cup , is having a huge year. She also released a Barbie Doll that debuted in July amid a career year with the Dream.

The forward, selected out of LSU with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2024 draft by the Chicago Sky , is averaging a double-double for the third consecutive season, bolstered by a career-high 16.5 points, 12.4 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.8 steals through 41 games. She leads the league in total rebounds, offensive rebounds (5.1 per game) and double-doubles (30). Reese is also third in steals per game.

"Angel is smashing double-double records. All the rebound records, single-game rebound records. She's having the best season of her career. From All-W perspectives, she should be on that. Defensive team. Defensive player of the year," Dream head coach Karl Smesko said on Sept. 17.

Reese hit the big number with her fifth rebound at the 1:53 mark of the first half. She created the rebound opportunity by blocking a layup attempt by Chicago's Gabriela Jaquez.

The three-time All-Star finished with 23 points and 10 rebounds, adding 4 assists, 2 steals and 3 blocks. She extended her record of double-doubles in a season with 31. Reese has also recorded double-digit rebounds in 16 consecutive games.
